meta.title: The ¥100 Umbrella
meta.sub: in which an assistant does everything wrong
meta.logline: Haru's first week as Nana's assistant: too many bags, a bus, a konbini, a prank that backfires, a bookshop owner who mocks him, and a ¥100 umbrella in the rain.

shots.text: Fine. A bet's a bet. One bag of candy. You got a job in one day. Nobody gets a job in one day.
Thank you, Kenta! Do you want half?
You're supposed to gloat. Winners gloat.
I don't know how. I'll eat it slowly instead. That's like gloating, but quieter.
Mister Mishima! An assistant needs a tie. This was mine, in nineteen eighty-two.
It has ducks on it.
Serious ducks. Business ducks. Go and make your rent.
You're late. And what is that tie?
Ducks. Serious business ducks. Mister Kobayashi says they mean I'm reliable.
Today's duties. Carry my bags. Hold my coffee. Don't speak unless I'm bored. Don't faint.
How will I know when you're bored?
You'll know. I sigh. It's very expensive-sounding.
Okay, okay. Ten thousand yen says the duck man cries before Friday.
Twenty says he cries before lunch!
I'd like to bet too, please. I bet I don't cry. I don't have twenty thousand yen, but I have half a bag of candy.
Deal. Candy man is in.
Can I ask you something, candy man? Why are you really here?
Because Nana hired me. And because Mister Kobayashi says rent is due on the first.
Everybody who comes up here wants something from her. Money. Followers. A selfie for their mother.
I'd like a selfie for my grandmother, actually. She's never seen a penthouse. She'll think it's a very tall lighthouse.
...Fine. That's weirdly acceptable.
Nana, I can't see. I think I'm wearing a shoe box.
Assistants don't see. Assistants carry.
The lady in the shop has been standing on high heels for nine hours. She hides it, but her feet hurt. Can we buy her a chair?
You want me to buy the shop girl a chair?
Just a small chair. You're buying everything else.
Fine. Buy her a chair. Put it on my card. And don't tell anyone I did that.
A secret chair! The best kind.
Pick anything you want for yourself. My treat.
I already have a cardigan.
Where is my car? Where is my driver?
Mister Sato? His daughter has a piano recital at eleven. I told him I'd make sure you got home.
You gave my driver the day off? You've worked for me for two hours!
She's playing Chopin. She practised for six months. He was going to miss it for your shoes.
...How do we get home, then?
The bus! It's very exciting. It has a bell.
People just... sit here? Together? With strangers?
That's the best part. Everybody's going somewhere different, but for twenty minutes we're all going the same way.
That's the most ridiculous thing I've ever heard.
Look, the man in the hat is going to the hospital, with flowers. The girl with the cello is late for a lesson. And that lady is asleep, and she'll wake up exactly at her stop. They always do.
How do you know all that?
I don't. I'm guessing. It's the best game on a bus. You try.
Fine. That man is going to buy a very ugly cardigan. Because he saw yours and got jealous.
You can press the bell when it's our stop. It's the most important job on the bus.
I pressed it! Haru, I pressed it! It went ding!
Young lady, you pressed that bell beautifully. Have a candy. My grandson used to love pressing it too.
A stranger gave me a candy. On a bus. Haru, is this normal?
On buses it is. It's the law of buses.
You were perfect. A very professional ding.
It was, the bus driver said later, the most excited anyone had ever been about his bell.
What is this place? Everything is so small and bright. Is this a museum?
It's a konbini. It's open twenty-four hours. If you're awake at three in the morning, it's awake with you.
There's hot food in a glass box! Who thought of that? Give them a medal!
Two rice balls, please. Salmon for me, and tuna mayonnaise for the lady, because she seems like a tuna mayonnaise person.
How dare you. ...I am, though.
Oh, it's raining. Wait here!
One umbrella, please. The clear kind. It's a hundred yen.
You bought the cheapest umbrella in Japan.
It's a very good umbrella. You can see the rain through it. Expensive umbrellas hide the sky.
Haru. Where are your parents? You talk about your grandmother, and a goat, and never about them.
They're very busy people in Osaka. They make bridges. When I kept fainting, they said the island would be good for me, and that they'd visit in the summer.
Did they?
They sent postcards. Every summer, a postcard of a bridge. I have twenty-one bridges. They're very good bridges.
Mine send cars. Every birthday, a car with a bow on it.
Then we're the same. We both got a lot of transport and not very much visiting.
That's the saddest thing anyone's ever said to me in a konbini. Pass the tuna mayonnaise.
It's your tuna mayonnaise. I bought it for you.
I know. I just wanted you to pass me something.
Mister Mishima! I'm a talent scout. I've got a job for you. Modelling. For a catalogue of... idiots.
Taku? Is that you in sunglasses?
No. I'm Mister Tanaka. Professional scout. Do you want the job or not?
That's very kind of you, Mister Tanaka. But I already have a job, and I'm not very good at it, so I should keep trying.
Also, I heard your music on Nana's phone. The slow song at the end, with the rain in it. It was sad and very good. You should make more like that.
Nobody listens to the end of that one. Everybody skips it.
I didn't. I listened to it four times.
...Man. I can't prank you. That's not fair.
So? How was day three of the assistant? Any crying?
Taku cried, and I won twenty thousand yen. I also bought a chair for a shop lady and gave a driver the day off.
And you weren't fired?
Not yet. Nana pressed the bell on the bus. She was very good at it.
I've got information. About the birthday party. It costs one rice ball.
Here. Salmon.
The crypto guy, Ryuji Gozen. My cousin parks cars at the hotel. He says Gozen asked about you. He says Gozen asked how much you cost.
A man like that thinks everything has a price, Mister Mishima. Be careful.
That's all right. I'm very cheap. Nine hundred yen, plus a bow.
We're closing. Also, cardigans that old belong in a museum, not in my shop.
That's all right. I like museums. I'm looking for a present for a friend's birthday. I have one thousand yen.
A thousand yen. For a girl?
For Nana. She has everything, so I thought she might like a book. Books are the only things you can have twice: once when you read them, and once when you remember them.
...Did you read that somewhere?
No, I just thought it. Is it wrong?
It's annoyingly right. Fine. Over here. A photo book of sunsets, slightly damaged. Nine hundred yen.
Oh no. Oh, they're so beautiful.
Are you fainting? In my shop? Over a damaged book?
Only a little. Could you wrap it? With a bow? I'll pay you the other hundred yen for the bow.
You're ridiculous.
You have a book by Dostoevsky in the window. The Idiot. Have you read it?
It's a shop, not a library. I sell them, I don't read them.
It's about a prince who is so kind that everybody decides he must be stupid. I read it eleven times. It made me feel less alone.
A prince who's so kind everyone thinks he's an idiot? Sounds like nobody I know.
He's ridiculous. I'm going to read that book about the prince he mentioned. Not because of him. For the shop.
Taku says you made him cry. He says it was your fault.
Oh no! Does that mean I lost the bet?
The bet was that you would cry, idiot. You won. You won twenty thousand yen and half a bag of candy.
I'll buy everyone rice balls!
My birthday's tomorrow. Twenty-five. Mister Togashi will stand up with a microphone and sell me to a man with a gold tooth.
You don't have to say yes to anybody.
In my family, nobody says no. We say, let me think about it, and then we say yes.
Then practise with me. Say no to something. Say no to this umbrella.
That's stupid.
Go on.
No. ...No! No to your hundred yen umbrella!
That was a beautiful no. Again!
No! No to Mister Togashi! No to the board! No to ducks on ties!
Not the ducks!
It was the first time in a very long time that Nana Kurosaki had laughed without checking who was watching.
Who is that idiot under her umbrella?
Tomorrow I'll find out what he costs.

Next time on Beautiful Idiot: Nana's birthday party! There's cake, a fireplace, a very large briefcase, and a game where everyone confesses their worst thing. A Hundred Million Yen. I'll bring the sunsets.
